Time-resolved (sliding-window) respiration-locked HF power.

Source: R/compute_hrv_freq_windowed.R
compute_hrv_freq_windowed.Rd

Same underlying method as compute_hrv_freq() (RR intervals resampled to an even grid, spectral power integrated in a band centered on the infant's own respiratory frequency), but instead of averaging across the whole recording into one number, computes HF power in sliding windows, giving a time series that can be compared against another time-varying signal (e.g. the Kuramoto synchrony trace from dynR::leida_pipeline()) within the same recording.

Usage

compute_hrv_freq_windowed(
  qrs,
  resp_signal,
  fs,
  window_sec = 60,
  step_sec = 15,
  resample_hz = 4,
  band_halfwidth_hz = 0.1,
  resp_search_range_hz = c(0.3, 2.5)
)

Arguments

qrs

An mrpheus_qrs object (output of detect_qrs()).

resp_signal

Numeric vector, the raw respiration channel.

fs

Sampling rate (Hz) of resp_signal.

window_sec

Window length in seconds. Default 60s: long enough for ~0.017 Hz frequency resolution (1/window_sec), comfortably finer than the 0.2 Hz-wide integration band, short enough to give reasonable temporal resolution over a ~15 minute scan.

step_sec

Step between window centers in seconds. Default 15s (75% overlap between consecutive windows).

resample_hz

RR-interval resampling rate. Default 4 Hz.

band_halfwidth_hz

Half-width of the integration band. Default 0.1 Hz.

resp_search_range_hz

Plausible respiratory frequency range for the whole-recording frequency detection. Default c(0.3, 2.5).

Value

A list: time (window center times, seconds, from recording start), hf_power (HF power at each window), resp_freq_hz, band_low, band_high.

Details

The respiratory frequency (and therefore the integration band) is detected once from the whole recording's resp channel and held fixed across all windows, rather than re-detected per window: a single spectral estimate from the whole recording is far more stable than one from a 60-second segment, and respiratory rate is generally stable within a single scan session for a sleeping/sedated infant. If that assumption doesn't hold for a given recording (e.g. a clear rate change partway through), this will misrepresent windows far from the global rate, worth checking the QC plot of resp_freq_hz if a session's within-scan behaviour is in question.

Verified against synthetic data: a ramping RSA amplitude trajectory (rising vagal tone over a 15-minute recording) is recovered with r=0.998 between windowed HF power and the true underlying amplitude-squared trajectory.
